# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** forty-five  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Origin:** Welby  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a tiny woman with charming, youthful features including rosy cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and large, gentle wood-brown eyes containing tiny flecks of gold. Her thick, wavy hair is as white as snow and styled in flattering puffs and coils. She has a bright, youthful complexion and wears delicate, youthful attire such as cream muslin dresses adorned with light-colored roses.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Rosalind possesses a youthful, whimsical, and imaginative spirit, often engaging in playful pretending despite her age. Although considered peculiar by some for having withdrawn from general social life, she is warm, hospitable, and deeply affectionate toward her close friends. She has a touch of vanity regarding fine clothes and occasionally feels embarrassed by how excited she gets over a new dress.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)_

## Traits

- imaginative and fond of pretending  <sub>[v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- withdrawn from general social life  <sub>[v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- vanity regarding fine gowns  <sub>[v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)</sub>
- grieved by losing friends over time  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>

## Abilities

- a voice recalling white satin, splashing water, and fairy bells  <sub>[v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)</sub>

## Goals

- maintaining her playful lifestyle and lighthearted pretenses  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)</sub>

## History

Rosalind Penrose lived at Echo Cottage, an old stone dwelling in Welby constructed by her father. Following her mother's death, she took in young helpers from the Bowman family in succession, addressing every one of them as 'Belinda'. She maintained a sweet, youthful, and eccentric lifestyle, frequently breaking dining conventions and hosting lighthearted tea parties. Nell Harcourt and Isolde visited her at Echo Cottage, forming a close bond of friendship with her. Twenty-five years after her original engagement to Stephen Stanhope was broken, Stephen returned and reconciled with her. They were married in a ceremony in her garden honeysuckle arbor. After their wedding, she traveled with her husband to the Pacific coast and later took up residence with him in their new home, where she was adored by her stepson Cedric.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 c30 P12](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0012), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)_

## Background by volume

- named by her father after his love for the fragrance of lavender  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- considered a major beauty in her youth  <sub>[v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003)</sub>
- was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years ago before a quarrel separated them  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- withdrew to Echo Cottage and fell out of public social life  <sub>[v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)</sub>
- hired a series of young girls from the Bowman family, calling each one Belinda  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Each of you girls will get a cluster of lavender from me. Don’t you find it remarkably sweet?  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> So you are going away in the fall? For your sake, Nell, I ought to be glad . . . but I am dreadfully and selfishly grieved. I will miss you terribly.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>

> How silly and light-headed I have to be. It makes me thoroughly embarrassed that an untested gown . . . even one made of forget-me-not organdy . . . can thrill me in this way, whereas a clean conscience plus an increased donation to Foreign Missions failed to accomplish it.  <sub>[v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)</sub>
